text: To make his dream come true, Nikolai began to save every kopeck, eating poorly, dressing like a beggar, and putting all his money in the bank. <break time="0.8s" /> He studied the newspaper advertisements for country estates every day, and in every farm he imagined there were always, without fail, a few gooseberry bushes. <break time="0.8s" /> Years passed, and he grew older and grayer, yet the dream never left him, and the money in his bank account kept growing slowly but steadily. <break time="0.8s" /> When he was no longer young, Nikolai married an elderly, unattractive widow, not out of love, but because she had saved a fair amount of money. <break time="0.8s" /> He kept her half starved, putting her money in the bank under his own name, and she, who had once lived comfortably, slowly grew pale and thin. <break time="0.8s" /> Within three years she died, yet Nikolai never for a moment believed he was to blame, for, as Ivan Ivanych said, money, like vodka, can make a man strange. <break time="0.8s" /> At last Nikolai bought an estate of about three hundred acres, a mortgaged property that had no orchard, no duck pond, and not a single gooseberry bush. <break time="0.8s" /> Through it flowed a river whose water was the color of coffee, because a brickworks and a factory for burning bones stood along its banks. <break time="0.8s" /> Nikolai did not seem to mind in the least, and he immediately ordered twenty gooseberry bushes, planted them, and settled down to live as a landowner.
